affected_system: food access, environmental health inspection, and community protection
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand
pair seasonal event- and market-conditioned workload forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Food outlets, inspections, assistance, prices, access, and environmental complaints have separate semantics.
Area food access is not treated as individual diet, food security, or health outcome.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand.

constraints.description: The food access and environmental health forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: environmental health commissioner and food-access program director
decision_question: What seasonal inspection, complaint, market-disruption, and assistance workload should operations prepare for?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The food access and environmental health forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: seasonal event- and market-conditioned workload forecasting
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority service demand above staffed capacity

intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority service demand above staffed capacity
distributional gap in priority service demand above staffed capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call forecast cases verified violations, illness, or food insecurity.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for environmental-health inspection and food-assistance demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

title: Forecast inspection and food-assistance service demand
transportability_risks: Retail markets, informal food systems, inspection law, mobility, prices, and eligibility vary.
Administrative participation can understate eligible need.
